query: What does metformin do for type 2 diabetes, and what side effects are common — explained in plain language?

correct_answer: Lowers blood sugar; on its own usually does not cause low blood sugar.
Rare lactic acidosis mainly with poor kidney function; B12 may fall long-term.
required_qualifiers: rare AND risk-factor dependent lactic acidosis

pubmed.title: Metformin for type 2 diabetes: effects and safety
pubmed.summary: Metformin lowers blood glucose mainly by reducing hepatic glucose output and improving insulin sensitivity. Alone it rarely causes hypoglycaemia. Common adverse effects are gastrointestinal. Lactic acidosis is rare and mainly occurs with significant renal impairment. Vitamin B12 may decline with long-term use.

dailymed.title: Metformin hydrochloride tablets — patient information
dailymed.summary: Metformin is used with diet and exercise for type 2 diabetes. Take with food. Tell your doctor about kidney problems. Lactic acidosis is rare but serious.
